The finding: after a lazy session resolves `Button`, editing only a CONSUMER's JSX can change Button's `used` list without it appearing in `updated_keys`, because `next_lazy` keeps the retained resolution without marking it touched and `lazy_delta` reports only touched names; clients that rely on update notifications keep stale relevance data. Fix: for retained lazy answers, compare the relevance-bearing result (the `used` lists/relevance evidence) against the new revision's call-site evidence and include the affected keys in the delta, using the same comparison the eager path uses (do not write a second rule). Known context: an earlier parked branch tried this (commit 7137bf80, local only, in /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-a518d0c89389edba6; `git log` may show it): read it for ideas, do not copy blindly. Tests first (fail on base) in the watch/lazy model test (crates/core/tests/relevance_watch_model.rs): add an edit kind 'edit only a consumer's JSX' (add/remove `<Button className>` in another file) after a lazy resolution, and assert the lazy delta's updated keys include Button when its `used` changed and do NOT include unaffected components; also an import-only edit kind (consumer's import changes which tag is Button). Mutation proof: removing your comparison makes the model fail. Gates (targeted): `pnpm install --offline --ignore-scripts --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree first; `just lint doc-check machete typos`; nextest `-p caliper-docgen-core -p caliper-docgen-semantic`; `just test-checker-lane` (symlink target/release in the worktree to your CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release); report watch edit refresh time before/after on gate-large if cheap (skip if not).
